verdict: Avoid new tobacco and bidi exposure in Guntur; the data call is Avoid and the news flow is worse, so only existing, fully-secured, invoice-backed lines may be renewed.
title: Guntur Tobacco Products & Bidi: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Guntur runs on FCV tobacco leaf, not on branded cigarettes.** The chain is farmer to auction platform to leaf trader/redryer to cigarette or bidi maker, and cash sits at the auction floor, not in the factory. The Tobacco Board sits here and farmers protest at its Guntur office over permission to sell excess and unauthorised produce [2]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's cash actually comes from auction realisations or from a buyer contract; if neither is documented, ask for the last three auction settlement statements.**

## What has changed now
**Leaf prices have fallen, and the Centre has had to permit sale of excess FCV tobacco while releasing relief to farmers [1][2][3].** That is a direct hit to trader and redryer margins and to farmer repayment capacity. On the demand side, peer Godfrey Phillips reported Q1FY27 net profit down 44%, revenue down 18.9% to Rs 1,205.5 crore from Rs 1,486.2 crore, on lower cigarette volumes and higher tobacco taxation [4][5][6]. **Management itself says it is phasing price increases to soften the consumer impact [7] — that means the maker absorbs the tax, and it squeezes everyone upstream.** Note the peer results are July 2026 and the rating report on a bidi manufacturer is from August 2020, so treat it as background only [10].

## The macro backdrop
**Andhra Pradesh GST collections are -0.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 6.3 pp gap [D].** India-wide, IIP for NIC 12 is -8.0% YoY and -4.4% Apr-to-date, and exports are -15.2% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. **Local news on Guntur is thin beyond the auction and relief stories, so lean on first principles and the peer set.**

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue only leaf redryers and threshers with owned godowns, a named buyer contract, and no auction-price speculation.** Avoid pure traders who buy at auction on hope, and avoid bidi units with no brand and no GST-clean sales. **Structure as a cash-flow line against assigned buyer receivables, with a stock-and-receivables charge and a promoter guarantee; take auction settlement statements and godown stock statements every month, and GST returns monthly.** If the borrower cannot show buyer-wise ageing, ask for the buyer's purchase order and last payment advice.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for auction realisations falling below the borrower's stated cost, stock ageing past one season, and GST turnover dropping faster than the state's -0.2% [D].** If a borrower asks to fund excess or unauthorised leaf purchases, decline — that is exactly the exposure the Centre had to regularise [2]. **Any request to stretch receivables beyond the buyer's stated credit terms is a signal to reduce, not renew.**
watch: realisation below borrower's stated cost -> freeze fresh limits and re-price
stock older than one season -> demand reduction or exit
turnover falling faster than AP's -0.2% [D] -> cut limit
ageing beyond stated credit terms -> stop renewal
